sections.html:
Syracuse sits in northern Davis County on the Great Salt Lake's east shore, roughly 30 miles north of Salt Lake City, between the lake and Interstate 15. It covers about 10 square miles at 4,272 feet. West Point is to the north, Clearfield to the east and northeast, and Layton to the southeast. A causeway off State Route 127 links the city to Antelope Island State Park, and Syracuse bills itself the Gateway to Antelope Island.

Buyers like the lake and island access. The land on the west side has wetlands that limit what can be built there.

The city has grown quickly: 4,658 residents in 1990, 9,398 in 2000, 24,331 in 2010 and 32,141 in 2020, with a July 1, 2025 estimate of 39,909. Owners occupy about 89.7% of homes, and median value for 2020 to 2024 is $573,300, with 3.64 people per household. That value is a survey figure, not an appraisal of your house. Since so much was built during that run, the age of the roof, water heater and furnace matters more than the age of the neighborhood.

The West Davis Corridor, State Route 177, opened on January 6, 2024. It runs northwest through Syracuse with interchanges at 2000 West and Antelope Drive. The first section is 16 miles long, from Farmington to West Point, and cost $750 million.

The road changed how people move around the west side of the county, and it raised interest in nearby land. Syracuse is pursuing a 169-acre redevelopment area, the WDC Gateway Community Reinvestment Area, at Antelope Drive and 3000 West, for housing, retail and commercial use. The city reports a significant increase in interest since the highway opened. The land is mostly farmed or undeveloped and needs wetland mitigation, which the city calls a significant hurdle. UDOT plans a 2.5-mile extension north to 1800 North in West Point, with work running through 2027.

Whether new development nearby helps or hurts a sale depends on the buyer. A cash buyer looks at the house as it stands today.

Syracuse has hot summers and a real winter. Highs often reach 95 degrees, and the area gets about 24 inches of precipitation and about 39 inches of snow a year, with monsoon thunderstorms from late July to mid-September. Roofs, gutters and grading take a beating, and snow load and freeze-thaw cycles are hard on older decks, driveways and sprinkler lines.

  • Check the roof and flashing after winter and after monsoon season.
  • Look at grading near the foundation, because snowmelt and rain need somewhere to go.
  • Have the sprinkler lines blown out each fall before a hard freeze.

Syracuse is in the Davis School District, and the city also has the Syracuse Arts Academy charter campuses, which are public schools with their own enrollment. Syracuse High School opened in 2007, Syracuse Junior High dates to 1960, and elementary schools include Cook (1979), Syracuse Elementary (1968), Bluff Ridge (1999) and Buffalo Point (2008). Families usually ask about boundaries first, so look yours up before you list.

sections.h2: Garage sales and home business rules
sections.html:
Chapter 10.35 of the city code covers home businesses and temporary sales, which matters if you are clearing out a house. A garage or yard sale needs no license for up to three consecutive days, and you can hold up to four such events a year.

  • Minor home occupations are allowed in residential zones if they use no more than 300 square feet or 20% of the floor area.
  • Home occupation permits are not transferable and end when the applicant stops living at the address, so a buyer must apply again.
  • A business license is required unless the business is exempt under state law.

If you run a daycare, salon or similar business from the house, tell the buyer the permit does not carry over. For anything else, contact Syracuse City planning for current rules.

sections.h2: Davis County property taxes and appeals
sections.html:
Taxes are due November 30, and if that date falls on a weekend or holiday it moves to the next business day. A late payment draws a 2.5% penalty or $10, whichever is greater. Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, up to one acre.

StepTiming
Valuation notice mailedEnd of July
Appeal to the county Board of EqualizationBy September 15 each year, so file early
Taxes dueNovember 30
Late penalty2.5% or $10, whichever is greater

You can appeal only the market value, not the tax rate. Evidence can be closing documents, a certified appraisal, three or more comparable sales or proof of an error in the assessor's data. Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington, 801-451-3331. Your title company prorates the current bill at closing.

An unpaid bill does not end a sale, but it has to be settled at closing. The title company asks the county for the balance, takes it from your proceeds, and divides the current year between you and the buyer. Mention any delinquency to the title officer at the start. If your valuation looks too high, the September 15 appeal date still applies while you are under contract, and a lower value reduces your share of the year's tax.

sections.h2: What to bring to a Syracuse closing
sections.html: Bring photo ID, the payoff statement from your lender if you have a mortgage, the latest tax notice, any permit paperwork for finished basements or additions, and every key, garage opener and gate code. If a home occupation permit was issued for the address, tell the buyer it ends with your move. Clear out the garage and yard before the final walk-through, using the up-to-three-day sale allowance if you want to sell off belongings.

Sellers who contact us usually need to move quickly: a job move, a divorce, a family that has outgrown the house, or an inherited property nobody wants to keep. A listing works well for a clean, updated house. If yours needs work, or you want to skip showings and a long wait, a cash offer is a simple comparison.

We buy as-is and you choose the closing date. Ask for an offer, set it against what a listing would net after commissions and repairs, and say no if it does not work. A title company handles payoffs and the tax proration, and you leave the signing with the balance. Bring photo ID, payoff details, the latest tax notice and the keys.

faqs.q: How many people live in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 39,909 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 32,141, so the city grew by more than 7,000 people in five years.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Syracuse, Utah?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $573,300 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey estimate, not an appraisal of your house.

faqs.q: When are Davis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. After it, a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater, applies.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Syracuse property valuation?
faqs.a: Yes. Davis County mails valuation notices at the end of July, and appeals are due by September 15. You can appeal only the market value, with evidence such as comparable sales or an appraisal.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a garage sale in Syracuse?
faqs.a: No license is needed for up to three consecutive days, with a limit of four events per year, under city code chapter 10.35.
